paite: Khedap tung nei lou ah na khepekte kilawm hi na mahmah e, Aw kumpi tanu; na phei guhtuah suangmantam bang ahi ua, nasem mipil khut nasep bang.
heading: Pasal
english: How beautiful are your feet in sandals, prince’s daughter! Your rounded thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a skillful workman.

paite: Na lai noubem bang ahi, huai ah uain hel akitasam ngei kei a; na gilpi huit buh hum lili pak siat dim abang hi.
english: Your body is like a round goblet, no mixed wine is wanting. Your waist is like a heap of wheat, set about with lilies.

paite: Na nawi zuktal nou nih phik abang uhi.
english: Your two breasts are like two fawns, that are twins of a roe.

paite: Na ngawng saiha insang abang; na mitte Barthrabbim kongpi a, Heshbon a om dilte abang uh; na nak Lebanon a insang abang a Damaskas lam muhsukna om.
english: Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like the pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bathrabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.

paite: Na tung a na lutang Karmel abang a, na lu a sam sandup abang; huai sampha lak ah kumpipa sal a mat in a-om hi.
english: Your head on you is like Carmel. The hair of your head like purple. The king is held captive in its tresses.

paite: Aw it, kipahna ding in nak kilawm in nak nop hi na mahmah chia!
english: How beautiful and how pleasant you are, love, for delights!

paite: Na sandan tum sing bang ahi a, na nawite grep gahbomte bang.
english: This, your stature, is like a palm tree, your breasts like its fruit.

paite: tum sing ah ka kaltou ding a, huai a hiangte ka len ding, ka chi a; na nawi grepgui gahbom bang hi henla, huan na nawi gim epul bang;
english: I said, “I will climb up into the palm tree. I will take hold of its fruit.” Let your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the smell of your breath like apples.

paite: Na kam uain hoihpen pen abang hi. Numei' Ka ngaihnou a dia nemtak a paisuk, ihmute muk a tolh paisuak.
english: Your mouth is like the best wine, that goes down smoothly for my beloved, gliding through the lips of those who are asleep.

paite: Ka ngaihnou a ka hi a, adeihlam kei lam ah a-om.
english: I am my beloved’s. His desire is toward me.

paite: Hong in, ka ngaihnou, gam ah i paikhe ding a; khoneute ah i giak ding.
english: Come, my beloved! Let’s go out into the field. Let’s lodge in the villages.

paite: Grephuan lam ah zingkhang in i thou ding a; Grepgui apakmumta hia, apakpalh akihongta hia i va en ding, huan theibuhfai apakkheta hia; huai ah ka itna ka hon pe ding hi.
english: Let’s go early up to the vineyards. Let’s see whether the vine has budded, its blossom is open, and the pomegranates are in flower. There I will give you my love.

paite: Zawlzongpak in gimnamtui asuaksak a, ka kongkhak uah thei manpha chikim, athak leh alui a-om, nang a ding in ka na kholkhawm, aw ngaihnou.
english: The mandrakes produce fragrance. At our doors are all kinds of precious fruits, new and old, which I have stored up for you, my beloved.
